steps: Draw nitrogen as the central atom, joined to three oxygen atoms; join one of these oxygen atoms to hydrogen.
Show one N=O double bond and single bonds from N to the other two oxygen atoms.
Use dots for oxygen electrons and crosses for nitrogen and hydrogen electrons. Show each covalent bond as a shared (×•) pair.
Show two lone pairs on the oxygen in O—H, two lone pairs on the double-bonded oxygen, and three lone pairs on the singly bonded oxygen.
Mark the central nitrogen N⁺ and the singly bonded terminal oxygen O⁻.

steps: Metals consist of positive metal ions arranged in a regular pattern, surrounded by a sea of mobile, delocalised electrons.
The strong electrostatic attraction between the positive ions and the delocalised electrons is called the metallic bond.
A large amount of energy is needed to overcome these strong metallic bonds; therefore, metals generally have high melting and boiling points.
The mobile electrons carry charge through the metal, so metals conduct electricity.
The mobile electrons also transfer thermal energy, so metals conduct heat.
When layers of positive ions slide past one another, the sea of electrons continues to hold the ions together; therefore, metals are malleable and ductile.
Metals are lustrous because their mobile electrons reflect light.
items.finalAnswer: Metallic bonding gives metals high melting and boiling points, electrical and thermal conductivity, malleability, ductility and lustre.
